source_name: Banka Slovenije - Katalog zbirk podatkov: Seznam notificiranih placilnih institucij (PDF)
why_relevant: Data-catalogue entry documenting the official dataset 'list of notified payment institutions' - tells you what fields BSI holds and under which legal basis, which is how you request or justify structured extraction.

source_name: Rekono–Bankart partnership announcement (identity/trust services)
why_relevant: Concrete, dated example of Bankart signing a technology partnership (remote identification and e-transaction trust services with Rekono). Template case for how Bankart partnerships surface — via its own site rather than the partner's — and a lead into the SI eID/trust-service vendor cluster.

source_name: Delavska hranilnica PSD2 API product pages on Bankart hub (SRC PSD2 API Collection)
why_relevant: Strongest single weak-signal example found: the API product description names the 'SRC PSD2 API Collection' — i.e. the Slovenian integrator SRC d.o.o. as the implementation vendor behind a bank's PSD2 interface. Exactly the kind of vendor exposure that never appears in press releases.

source_name: Bankart — 'Opis placilnih sistemov za procesiranje SEPA transakcij' (PDF)
why_relevant: Formal scheme documentation describing SIMP-PS and BIPS operation, participant roles and governance (e.g. SIMP committee composition). High-density technical/structural source naming system participants and rules.

source_name: FURS (Financial Administration) news – 'Prenehanje delovanja mBills'
why_relevant: State-agency notice about mBills ceasing to be an eDavki payment option, listing which wallets remain accepted (Flik, VALÚ) — an authoritative, non-marketing indicator of wallet viability and of which rails the public sector supports.

source_name: Smernice za javno naročanje informacijskih rešitev (MJU/GZS)
why_relevant: Official guidelines for procuring IT solutions define the standard vocabulary and lot structures Slovenian public buyers use when tendering banking/core-IT systems — a glossary source that improves keyword recall on the notice portals.

source_name: ZBS letno poročilo (annual report) – event and working-group record
why_relevant: Retrospective, dated record of which conferences, consultations and working groups ZBS actually ran, with counts and themes — lets a collector reconstruct historical event series that no longer have live pages.

source_name: Delo.si – payments and banking reporting
why_relevant: National daily covering the bank-side response to fintech competition (instant-payment app rollout, regulatory clearance for Flik); useful for chronology and for named institutional actors.

source_name: SRC d.o.o. — PSD2/open banking platform case study
why_relevant: Slovenian systems integrator publishing a named PSD2 platform case study for banks — an example of the local integrator layer adjacent to payments (API/open-banking gateways), and a template for the kind of case-study content SI IT firms publish about bank projects.

source_name: FinTech Futures — Bankart/Nets Slovenian payments central infrastructure story
why_relevant: Documents the vendor selection behind Slovenia's central SCT / SCT Inst infrastructure (Nets as technology supplier to Bankart). This is exactly the kind of go-live/vendor-award trace the cell targets, and FinTech Futures covers such awards across CEE consistently.

source_name: Forbes Slovenija (forbes.n1info.si) – payments business coverage
why_relevant: Carries quantified market data on Slovenian payment rails (reported Flik user and transaction volumes, share of online payments) and profiles of local payment startups — rare source of usable numbers.

source_name: Slovenian business/tech press coverage of bank core-system migrations (Forbes Slovenija, Necenzurirano, Žurnal24)
why_relevant: Slovene-language reporting on the BKS Bank core-banking/payments platform migration and its post-go-live failures. Migration incidents are a reliable 'reveals-indirectly' channel: they surface the existence, timing and often the supplier of a core replacement that no vendor advertises when it goes badly.

source_name: iVarnost.si – event reporting and award coverage
why_relevant: Slovenian security-media outlet that files post-event reports naming award recipients, sponsors and attendance figures; recovers detail that conference sites delete after the edition ends.

source_name: ivarnost.si — sector article profiling Bankart as leading SI payments solution provider
why_relevant: Slovenian security/technology outlet publishing vendor profiles that summarise Bankart's service portfolio and direction (open banking, instant payments, mobile, e-identity). Useful for narrative and strategy signals not present in corporate pages.

source_name: Monitor.si – IT magazine (fintech/wallet partnership coverage)
why_relevant: Reported the Petrol–mBills strategic tie-up; Monitor consistently covers wallet/merchant partnerships that never appear in English sources.

source_name: Temenos Success Stories / Customer Case Studies (incl. NLB success story)
why_relevant: Vendor-authored success story explicitly naming Nova Ljubljanska Banka (NLB), Slovenia's largest bank, as a Temenos core customer; contains deal scope detail (corporate core first, retail migration following N Banka migration) and vendor-claimed KPIs (time-to-market -50%, cost -25%). This is the single most detailed public record of the SI core-banking stack at the market leader.

source_name: ASEE newsroom – regional payments event coverage
why_relevant: ASEE (with Monri) co-founded Money Motion and publishes named post-event recaps listing co-sponsors (Nexi, Mastercard, OTP Bank, Payten). A direct competitor's own visibility record, dated and self-declared — the highest-signal form of sponsorship evidence.

entity_name: Chambers / CEE Legal Matters Slovenia M&A and Banking guides
source_name: Chambers / CEE Legal Matters Slovenia M&A and Banking guides
why_relevant: Annual practitioner surveys summarise completed and pending SI financial-sector deals plus regulatory-approval mechanics; good annual baseline and actor-map refresher.

source_name: EMIS CEE Fintech Sector Report
why_relevant: Commercial CEE sector report aggregating fintech company and deal data across the region including Slovenia; useful as a periodic structured cross-check on deal counts and named vendors rather than as a news feed.

entity_name: European Commission DG COMP merger case files
source_name: European Commission DG COMP merger case files (M.10075 Nexi/Nets)
why_relevant: Merger decisions contain detailed, evidence-based descriptions of acquiring/processing market structure and national shares, including CEE markets — one of the few sources with structural competitive data on acquirers.

source_name: Finance.si IKT-informator (sponsored ICT supplements)
why_relevant: Finance's periodic IKT-informator supplement is where Slovenian IT houses buy space to describe their solutions and name clients, including financial-sector ones. Copies are frequently re-hosted on vendor sites (as here on Mikrografija's), so the supplements are collectable even without a Finance subscription. Good longitudinal record of vendor positioning.

source_name: Holland FinTech — State of FinTech in the Adria Region
why_relevant: Association-published regional overview treating Adria (Slovenia, Croatia, BiH, Serbia) as one unit — a pointer to regional actors, associations and events that the country-only view misses.

source_name: Humanfrog case studies — Sberbank banka (SI digital project)
why_relevant: Regional digital agency/integrator publishing a named case study for a bank operating in Slovenia (Sberbank, subsequently absorbed by NLB). Shows the second tier of the vendor landscape — digital agencies and integrators — which often documents projects that platform vendors never publish.

source_name: Na Prostem – 'Suverenost uporabnika slovenskih mobilnih in spletnih bank'
why_relevant: Independent technical audit-style comparison of Slovenian mobile/online banking apps across institutions. Reveals platform characteristics and third-party dependencies (SDKs, identity providers) that banks never announce — an indirect way to infer the vendor behind an app.

source_name: SAOP help — 'Nastavitve za povezavo na ZZI: izmenjava e-računov z bankami in UJP'
why_relevant: Third-party ERP vendor documentation that confirms the ZZI–bank e-invoice integration path in operational detail. ERP/accounting help portals are a reliable indirect way to learn which banks expose which channels, because they must document real, working connections.

source_name: The Fintech Times — country/ecosystem deep dives (Slovenia, Croatia)
why_relevant: Publishes recurring country ecosystem features that name local players, banks and regulators in one place — cheap actor-map refresher for Slovenia and the wider Adriatic; verified Slovenia and Croatia 2026 pieces exist.

entity_name: UniCredit Bank Slovenia branch-renovation / self-service microsites
source_name: UniCredit Bank Slovenia branch-renovation / self-service microsites
why_relevant: Banks publish per-branch renovation microsites when they convert a branch to a new self-service format. These pages describe the new equipment and customer journey and are the closest thing to a public branch-automation case study in Slovenia - useful for inferring which vendor's format (recycler, video teller, assisted self-service kiosk) was chosen, and for benchmarking the pace of branch-automation conversion across the network.

source_name: Veeam customer stories — OTP banka (Slovenia)
why_relevant: Concrete confirmed example of the cell's core pattern outside core banking: an infrastructure vendor publishing a named Slovenian bank customer story (OTP banka, data protection for Microsoft 365). Establishes that infra/ISV customer-story pages are a productive vein for SI stack mapping and post-merger IT signals.

source_name: Vendor case-study pages naming Bankart (IBM, Nets/Nexi, fintech trade press)
why_relevant: Bankart is a buyer of vendor technology; suppliers publish the relationship when Bankart will not. IBM hosts a Bankart case study, and FinTech Futures reported a Bankart–Nets deal to deliver new payments infrastructure to the Slovenian banking sector. This class of page is the single best evidence of Bankart's technology stack and supplier set.
